name: Alfred
description: Keyboard launcher and Spotlight replacement with fast app/file launching, clipboard history, snippets, and a powerful Workflows automation engine; free core with a one-time Powerpack unlock.

name: Raycast
description: Keyboard-first launcher with a large extension store, built-in window management, and optional AI; free tier with a Pro subscription for AI and cloud sync.

name: Things 3
description: Award-winning task manager for Apple platforms with a famously polished design and reliable sync; one-time purchase per platform, no subscription.

name: OmniFocus
description: The power user's GTD task manager with projects, custom perspectives, and structured reviews; universal one-time license or optional subscription.

name: Fantastical
description: Calendar app with natural-language event parsing, menu-bar quick access, and integrated tasks; free tier with a Flexibits Premium subscription unlocking everything.

name: Spark
description: Smart email client with a unified inbox, snoozing, send-later, and AI writing help; free for individuals with paid team and premium plans.

name: Todoist
description: Cross-platform task manager with natural-language input, boards, filters, and 60+ integrations; free tier with a Pro subscription for power features.

name: Obsidian
description: Local-first Markdown knowledge base with bidirectional linking, graph view, and a huge community plugin ecosystem; free core with paid Sync/Publish and commercial tiers.

name: Bear
description: Beautiful Apple-only Markdown notes app with nested tags, cross-note links, and a Focus mode; free with a Bear Pro subscription for sync and full export.

name: Craft
description: Native Apple-ecosystem docs app with block editing, offline-first design, and AI writing assistance; generous free tier with affordable Plus/Family plans.

name: Ulysses
description: Distraction-free Markdown writing environment for long-form projects, with publishing integrations and style checking; subscription only.

name: iA Writer
description: Minimalist Markdown editor known for its focus mode and signature typography; one-time purchase per platform, no subscription.

name: Logseq
description: Privacy-first, open-source outliner knowledge base that stores plain local Markdown files; free and community-driven with no paywalled core.

name: Notion
description: All-in-one workspace for notes, docs, wikis, and databases with real-time collaboration; free tier with paid plans for heavier team use.

name: ForkLift
description: Dual-pane file manager with FTP/SFTP/WebDAV and cloud-service connections plus folder sync and batch rename; one-time license.

name: Path Finder
description: Long-running Finder replacement with dual-pane browsing, batch rename, folder sync, and a terminal drawer; subscription-first with a one-time license option.

name: Transmit
description: Panic's fast and beloved file-transfer client for FTP/SFTP/S3 with Panic Sync for server credentials; one-time purchase.

name: Cyberduck
description: Free, open-source FTP/SFTP/WebDAV/S3 browser with Cryptomator client-side encryption support; donation-supported development.

name: Commander One
description: Swift-built dual-pane file manager with a built-in FTP client, archive support, and a terminal emulator; free with a paid PRO Pack for advanced features.

name: HoudahSpot
description: Advanced file-search utility layering powerful multi-criteria filters, saved templates, and Quick Look on top of Spotlight; one-time license.

name: Mountain Duck
description: Mounts servers and cloud storage as local Finder volumes with smart sync and offline caching; one-time license from the Cyberduck team.

name: iStat Menus
description: Menu-bar system monitor for CPU, GPU, memory, network, sensors, fan speeds, and battery with customizable readouts; one-time purchase.

name: DaisyDisk
description: Gorgeous sunburst disk-space visualizer that finds storage hogs at a glance and deletes them with drag-and-drop; one-time license.

name: Macs Fan Control
description: Monitors temperature sensors and takes manual control of fan speeds with sensor-based rules; free version with a paid Pro license for full control.

name: OnyX
description: Veteran donationware maintenance utility exposing hidden macOS settings, cache cleaning, disk checks, and system scripts; free for over 20 years.

name: coconutBattery
description: Detailed battery health, cycle count, and capacity statistics for Macs and connected iDevices; free with a paid Plus edition for advanced data.

name: CleanMyMac
description: All-in-one Mac cleaner and optimizer with junk removal, Space Lens, and malware scanning; subscription-first with a one-time purchase option.

name: IINA
description: The modern open-source video player for macOS, built on mpv with a polished native Swift interface. Notable for its deep macOS integration: Picture-in-Picture, Force Touch, Touch Bar support, and a standalone music mode.

name: HandBrake
description: The veteran open-source video transcoder for converting almost any video format into modern MP4/MKV/WebM files. Still the go-to free tool for ripping and re-encoding video with full control over quality and file size.

name: OBS Studio
description: The industry-standard free and open-source app for screen recording and live streaming. Its scene composition, multi-track audio routing, and plugin ecosystem make it the default capture tool for tutorials and creators.

name: DaVinci Resolve
description: Blackmagic's all-in-one post-production suite for editing, color grading, VFX, and audio. The free tier is a full professional editor (no watermark), with Resolve Studio as a one-time upgrade for AI tools and 8K+ workflows.

name: Affinity
description: Canva's unified creative suite combining photo editing, vector design, and page layout in one app — free for individuals (AI tools need Canva Pro), a serious Adobe alternative. Formerly the paid Affinity Photo/Designer/Publisher trio from Serif.

name: Shottr
description: A tiny, blazing-fast screenshot utility built for designers and pixel-perfectionists. Its scrolling captures, OCR, annotation, and pixel ruler beat the built-in macOS tool at a fraction of competitors' prices.

name: Sketch
description: The Mac-native UI/UX design platform that defined the modern interface design workflow, with symbols, prototyping, and developer handoff. Available as a per-editor subscription or a $120 Mac-only one-time license.

name: Bitwarden
description: The trusted open-source password manager with unlimited passwords and devices on its free tier. Notable for full transparency — clients and server are auditable — plus optional self-hosting.

name: 1Password
description: The premium password manager known for its polished UX, Secret Key encryption model, and family/team vault sharing. Subscription-only, with Watchtower breach alerts and a full developer CLI.

name: KeePassXC
description: A fully offline, open-source password manager storing credentials in an encrypted local .kdbx file — no cloud, no ads, no subscriptions. The privacy-first choice for users who want total control of their vault.

name: Little Snitch
description: The classic Mac firewall that reveals and controls every outbound network connection per app, with DNS encryption and blocklists. The definitive tool for catching apps that phone home.

name: LuLu
description: Patrick Wardle's free, open-source outbound firewall from the Objective-See foundation — a lightweight, community-trusted alternative to Little Snitch. Blocks unknown outgoing connections with simple allow/deny alerts.

name: KnockKnock
description: Objective-See's free persistence scanner — like AutoRuns for macOS — that enumerates everything installed to survive reboots and flags known malware via VirusTotal. Essential for Mac malware triage.

name: Wipr 2
description: The beloved indie Safari content blocker by Kaylee Calderolla — blocks ads, trackers, cookie banners, and miners with zero configuration. One $4.99 purchase covers all Apple devices, with an optional Filtr add-on for system-wide blocking.

name: Polisher
description: Aaron Cross's free, local-first macOS writing assistant: system-wide proofreading, rewriting, inline suggestions, and autocomplete powered by an embedded local model. Fully private — no cloud, no subscriptions.

name: LM Studio
description: The most approachable way to discover, download, and chat with local LLMs on your Mac — no terminal required. Free for personal and commercial use, with a Hugging Face model catalog and OpenAI-compatible local server.

name: Jan
description: The open-source, fully offline ChatGPT alternative that runs local models via llama.cpp in a polished desktop UI. Notable for its OpenAI-compatible local API, MCP support, and optional cloud bridges.

name: Enchanted
description: An elegant, fully native SwiftUI chat app for talking to privately hosted models via your own Ollama server. Gives you a ChatGPT-style UI over your own hardware, with conversations stored on-device.

name: Superwhisper
description: System-wide AI voice dictation for Mac that types into any app, with context-aware modes and on-device models for offline privacy. Free tier never expires; Pro adds cloud models, file transcription, and meeting recording.

name: MacWhisper
description: A local-first transcription powerhouse by indie dev Jordi Bruin, running Whisper and Parakeet models on-device for files, meetings, and system-wide dictation. Free tier is generous; Pro is a one-time purchase with lifetime updates.

name: BoltAI
description: A truly native (SwiftUI/AppKit) multi-model AI workspace for Mac with chat, agents, document Q&A, and MCP tools. Bring-your-own-key across 300+ models, perpetual one-time license from $79.

name: Nova
description: Panic's native Mac code editor with a built-in terminal, Git client, and remote publishing. Designed with a Mac-like feel for web and general development.

name: Proxyman
description: Native, high-performance HTTP debugging proxy for macOS that lets developers observe and manipulate HTTP/HTTPS requests. Used for inspecting and intercepting app and API traffic.

name: TablePlus
description: Native, fast database management client for macOS supporting many SQL and NoSQL databases. Bundles a companion iOS client with the license.

name: Kaleidoscope
description: Native macOS app for comparing files, folders, and images with a polished visual diff interface. A long-standing favorite for code review and resolving merge conflicts.

name: Dash
description: Offline API documentation browser and code snippet manager for macOS. Bundles hundreds of docsets so reference material stays searchable without a network.

name: HTTPie Desktop
description: Desktop GUI for the HTTPie API client, aimed at visually testing and debugging REST APIs. Closed-source companion to the open-source HTTPie CLI.

name: Ghostty
description: Fast, native macOS terminal emulator written in Zig, focused on speed and native platform integration. A modern, GPU-accelerated alternative to iTerm2.

name: iTerm2
description: Long-standing, feature-rich terminal emulator for macOS and the most popular Terminal.app replacement. Supports split panes, search, autocomplete, and deep customization.

name: Starship
description: Minimal, fast, cross-shell prompt written in Rust that shows contextual info like git status and language versions. ISC-licensed and highly customizable.

name: Zellij
description: Modern terminal multiplexer written in Rust with built-in layouts and a plugin system. Positioned as a friendlier tmux alternative.

name: Oh My Zsh
description: Community-driven framework for managing zsh configuration, with hundreds of plugins and themes. The standard way most developers set up their macOS shell.

name: tmux
description: Terminal multiplexer that runs multiple shell sessions in one window, with detachable sessions that survive disconnects. A classic ISC-licensed Unix tool.

name: Rectangle
description: Open-source window management app that snaps and resizes windows with keyboard shortcuts or drag. Free core with an optional paid Pro tier.

name: Amethyst
description: Free, open-source automatic tiling window manager for macOS inspired by XMonad. Tiles windows into layouts automatically without manual dragging.

name: yabai
description: Open-source tiling window manager for macOS configured via shell scripting, popular with keyboard-driven power users. MIT-licensed and highly scriptable.

name: AeroSpace
description: i3-inspired tiling window manager for macOS with automatic tiling and workspaces. Sources are MIT-licensed.

name: Magnet
description: Simple window snapping app for macOS sold on the Mac App Store by CrowdCafe. Drag windows to screen edges or use shortcuts to snap them into place.

name: Moom
description: Window manager from Many Tricks that resizes and moves windows via hover menus, shortcuts, and custom layouts. One-time purchase.

name: Maccy
description: Lightweight, open-source clipboard manager for macOS written natively in Swift. Keeps a searchable history of everything you copy.

name: Ice
description: Free, open-source menu bar manager for macOS (GPL-3.0) that hides and organizes menu bar icons. Adds a second 'Ice Bar' for notched MacBooks.

name: Bartender
description: Menu bar organizer that hides, rearranges, and shows menu bar icons on demand. One-time purchase around $16, with a 4-week trial.

name: CleanShot X
description: Native screenshot and screen-recording utility for macOS with annotations, scrolling capture, and cloud sharing. One-time purchase.

name: Keyboard Maestro
description: Powerful macro and automation tool for macOS that can control nearly any app via hotkeys, triggers, and scripts. One-time purchase.
